# Widest Container — Explained, One Approach at a Time

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-explained.mjs from src/data/problems/two-pointers/container-water.ts.
     Edit the data, then run `npm run docs:explained`. Edits here are overwritten. -->

**Two Pointers** · medium · [the same question on LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/container-with-most-water/)

Given an array heights where heights[i] is the height of a vertical line at position i, choose two lines so the area between them (width × shorter height) is maximised. Return that area.

## What the input promises

- 2 <= height.length <= 10^5
- 0 <= height[i] <= 10^4
- the container is capped by the shorter line and widened by the distance between them
- the lines are vertical: nothing between them affects the area

## Examples

| Input | Output | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `heights = [1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]` | `49` | Lines of height 8 and 7, seven apart: 7 × 7 = 49. |

<details>
<summary>Hints, one nudge at a time — open them in order</summary>

1. Area is limited by the shorter line. Start with maximum width — both ends.
2. Shrinking width is always a loss unless the limiting side improves. Which pointer is pointless to move?
3. Moving the taller side can never help: width drops and the short side still caps the height. Always move the shorter one.

</details>

---

## 1. Brute force

Measure all pairs. Fine for tiny inputs; quadratic wall at scale. State it, then improve it.

```python
def max_area(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    best = 0
    for i in range(len(heights)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(heights)):
            best = max(best, (j - i) * min(heights[i], heights[j]))
    return best
```

**O(n²) time · O(1) space**
<details>
<summary>The same rung in Java</summary>

```java
public int maxArea(int[] h) {
    int best = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < h.length; i++)
        for (int j = i + 1; j < h.length; j++)
            best = Math.max(best, (j - i) * Math.min(h[i], h[j]));
    return best;
}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary>The same rung in C++</summary>

```cpp
int maxArea(const vector<int>& h) {
    int best = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)h.size(); i++)
        for (int j = i + 1; j < (int)h.size(); j++)
            best = max(best, (j - i) * min(h[i], h[j]));
    return best;
}
```

</details>

## 2. The one to remember

> **Why now.** Measuring every pair is n squared comparisons for one number. Moving the pointer at the shorter line inward discards only the pairs that line already capped, so a single sweep is enough.

Two pointers at the extremes. Record the area, then move the pointer at the shorter line inward — keeping it could only pair it with narrower widths while it stays the cap. This greedy discard is safe because every skipped pair is provably no better than one already measured.

```python
def max_area(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    i, j = 0, len(heights) - 1
    best = 0
    while i < j:
        best = max(best, (j - i) * min(heights[i], heights[j]))
        if heights[i] < heights[j]:
            i += 1
        else:
            j -= 1
    return best
```

**O(n) time · O(1) space**
<details>
<summary>The same rung in Java</summary>

```java
public int maxArea(int[] h) {
    int i = 0, j = h.length - 1, best = 0;
    while (i < j) {
        best = Math.max(best, (j - i) * Math.min(h[i], h[j]));
        if (h[i] < h[j]) i++;
        else j--;
    }
    return best;
}
```

</details>
<details>
<summary>The same rung in C++</summary>

```cpp
int maxArea(const vector<int>& h) {
    int i = 0, j = (int)h.size() - 1, best = 0;
    while (i < j) {
        best = max(best, (j - i) * min(h[i], h[j]));
        if (h[i] < h[j]) i++;
        else j--;
    }
    return best;
}
```

</details>

---

## The arc

One greedy argument carries the whole problem, and it is worth being able to say precisely: the area is limited by the SHORTER wall, so moving the taller one inward can never help — the width shrinks and the height is still capped by the short wall. Moving the shorter one is the only move that can improve anything, so no pair worth checking is ever skipped. That is the shape of every two-pointer proof: show that the pointer you advance cannot be part of a better remaining answer. Brute force is worth writing once to see the quadratic, and the exchange argument is worth rehearsing out loud, because an interviewer asking 'why is that safe?' is asking for exactly this paragraph.

| # | Approach | Cost | What it adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Brute force | O(n²) time · O(1) space | the baseline — nothing before it |
| 2 | The one to remember | O(n) time · O(1) space | Measuring every pair is n squared comparisons for one number. Moving the pointer at the shorter line inward discards only the pairs that line already capped, so a single sweep is enough. |

## Full runnable script

Every rung in one file, printed against the inputs `npm run verify:run`
drives the Java and C++ blocks with. Run it: `python explained.py`.

```python
def max_area_brute_force(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    best = 0
    for i in range(len(heights)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(heights)):
            best = max(best, (j - i) * min(heights[i], heights[j]))
    return best


def max_area_the_one_to_remember(heights: list[int]) -> int:
    i, j = 0, len(heights) - 1
    best = 0
    while i < j:
        best = max(best, (j - i) * min(heights[i], heights[j]))
        if heights[i] < heights[j]:
            i += 1
        else:
            j -= 1
    return best

APPROACHES = [
    max_area_brute_force,
    max_area_the_one_to_remember,
]

# the same inputs npm run verify:run drives the Java and C++ blocks with:
# the shorter wall deciding which pointer moves, including on a tie — [4,4,4,4]
CASES = [
    lambda: ([1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7],),
    lambda: ([1,1],),
    lambda: ([4,4,4,4],),
    lambda: ([0,2,0],),
    lambda: ([1,2,4,3],),
]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for fn in APPROACHES:
        answers = []
        for make in CASES:
            try:
                answers.append(fn(*make()))
            except BaseException as exc:  # a rung that raises names itself
                answers.append(f"!{exc}")
        print(f"{fn.__name__:<30} -> {answers}")
```
